explanation: The cubes take shape in the last stretch of the gut, where the wall stretches unevenly. Wombats leave them on rocks and logs, perhaps to mark their territory.

claims.text: Koalas, kangaroos and platypuses do not produce cube-shaped droppings.
Wombat faeces become cube-shaped in the final part of the intestine, where the gut wall has regions of different stiffness.
Wombats deposit their droppings on prominent objects such as rocks and logs, which may mark territory.
